title: Beetles and Birds: Natural Selection
subject: science
goal: Find out what happens to a beetle population when birds eat the beetles they can see best.
steps: Start with 10 green and 10 brown beetles on the brown "forest floor" (your desk). Record generation 0.
The birds hunt: roll the die 8 times. Each roll, take away one beetle as the table says.
Survivors have young: for each beetle left, add one beetle of the same color. Young look like their parents.
Record the new numbers of green and brown beetles. Pass the role cards to the left.
Repeat steps 2-4 for three generations, then answer the group question: what changed, and why?

dice.title: The bird hunts (brown beetles are hard to see on brown ground)
rows: A bird spots and eats a green beetle (if none are left, a brown one).
A bird spots and eats a brown beetle (if none are left, a green one).

listen_for: “The beetles turned brown to hide”: ask what color each young beetle is, and where its color came from.
Groups that see brown take over: ask what would happen on green moss instead.
debrief: Did any single beetle change color? What changed?
Which three things had to be true for the population to change? (Beetles differ, young look like parents, some survive more.)
What would happen if the forest floor turned green?
sources: The idea is the classic “bird and moth” camouflage lab, as in NOVA's Evolution Lab and PhET's Natural Selection simulation; the rules and questions here are Paper Loop's own.
